title: Replacing the encoded index tape
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let $x,v$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $v$ whose state is $s$. For any natural numbers $i,j$ and phases $\mathrm{ph},\mathrm{ph}'$, first form the encoded configuration from $c$ with index $i$ and phase $\mathrm{ph}$, then set its state to $(s,\mathrm{ph}')$, replace the extra tape by the tape containing the binary expansion of $j$, and put that tape's head at position $0$. The resulting configuration is exactly the encoded configuration from $c$ with index $j$ and phase $\mathrm{ph}'$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean words $x,v$ and a configuration $c$ on input $v$
